find:
# And it is held to exactly what the packaging job uploads, before
      # anything of it is used and before the notary's key exists: one disk
      # image in release/, the target's manifest in vendor/, both plain
      # files, and nothing else. No link, no third file, no other folder. A
      # name is shown quoted, so that nothing it holds is read by the runner
      # as a command.
      - name: Refuse a download that holds anything but the image and its manifest
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export LC_ALL=C
          root="$RUNNER_TEMP/signed"
          if [ -L "$root" ] || [ ! -d "$root" ]; then
            echo "::error::there is no folder where the signed image is unpacked, so there is nothing to notarise"
            exit 1
          fi
          image='^release/[A-Za-z0-9 ._-]+\.dmg$'
          images=0
          manifests=0
          refused=''
          while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            name="${entry#"$root"/}"
            printf -v quoted '%q' "$name"
            if [ -L "$entry" ]; then
              refused="$refused $quoted (a link)"
            elif [ -d "$entry" ]; then
              case "$name" in
                release|vendor) ;;
                *) refused="$refused $quoted (a folder)" ;;
              esac
            elif [ ! -f "$entry" ]; then
              refused="$refused $quoted (neither a file nor a folder)"
            elif [ "$name" = "vendor/manifest-$TARGET.json" ]; then
              manifests=$((manifests + 1))
            elif [[ "$name" =~ $image ]]; then
              images=$((images + 1))
            else
              refused="$refused $quoted"
            fi
          done < <(find "$root" -mindepth 1 -print0)
          if [ -n "$refused" ] || [ "$images" -ne 1 ] || [ "$manifests" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::the download is not what the packaging job uploads, which is one disk image in release/ and vendor/manifest-$TARGET.json: it holds $images disk image(s) and $manifests manifest(s)${refused:+, and besides them:$refused}. Nothing of it was used, and the notary's key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "the download holds one disk image and vendor/manifest-$TARGET.json, and nothing else"

      # The refusal above sees only what landed in the download's own
      # folder. This holds the workspace itself to the checkout, still
      # before the key exists: at this run's commit, the checked-out files
      # as that commit has them, and nothing beside them, ignored names
      # included. A file that reached the workspace by any road, an archive
      # unpacked outside its folder among them, stops the job here. Git is
      # told to take nothing from the folder it is judging that would run a
      # program: no file-system monitor, no external diff, no conversion.
      - name: Refuse a workspace that is not this run's checkout
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git() { command git -c core.fsmonitor=false "$@"; }
          head=$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)
          if [ "$head" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
            echo "::error::the workspace is at commit ${head:0:12} and this run is for ${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}: it is not this run's checkout. Nothing was run, and the notary's key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git diff --quiet --no-ext-diff --no-textconv HEAD --; then
            git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored
            echo "::error::a checked-out file is not as the commit has it: something wrote over a script or the config this job is about to use with the notary's key. Nothing was run, and the key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          stray=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored)
          if [ -n "$stray" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$stray"
            echo "::error::the workspace holds what the checkout did not put there (listed above), beside the files this job is about to use with the notary's key. Nothing was run, and the key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "the workspace is the checkout of ${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}: its files as committed, and nothing beside them"

      # spctl's verdicts mean nothing on a machine where Gatekeeper's
      # assessments are off: everything is accepted, signed or not. A runner
      # image can come that way, so they are turned on here if they are off,
      # the status is said before and after, and only a runner where they
      # will not come on fails. macOS has spelt the option two ways.
      - name: Turn Gatekeeper's assessments on if they are off
        shell: bash
        run: |
          before=$(spctl --status 2>&1 || true)
          echo "Gatekeeper before: $before"
          if [[ "$before" != *'assessments enabled'* ]]; then
            sudo spctl --global-enable || sudo spctl --master-enable || true
          fi
          after=$(spctl --status 2>&1 || true)
          echo "Gatekeeper after: $after"
          if [[ "$after" != *'assessments enabled'* ]]; then
            echo "::error::Gatekeeper's assessments are off on this runner and could not be turned on, so spctl's verdicts here would prove nothing about the image"
            exit 1
          fi

      # The notary's key exists in this step alone: written to a file nobody
      # else can read, handed to the script by path, and removed when the
      # shell exits normally or fails; on a cancelled or timed-out step the
      # hosted runner is discarded with the file. The limit is past the
      # script's own worst case, so the script gives up first and says why:
      # 70 minutes for the submission (notarytool's 60 of waiting and the
      # upload before it), three tries of the log and three of the staple at
      # 2 minutes each with a quarter of a minute between tries, and 1 for
      # the validation, which is 84.
      - name: Notarise and staple the disk image
        timeout-minutes: 90
        shell: bash
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY_P8: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_P8 }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          images=("$RUNNER_TEMP/signed/release/"*.dmg)
          if [ "${#images[@]}" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::expected one disk image in the download's release folder, found ${#images[@]}"
            exit 1
          fi
          umask 077
          key="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary-key.p8"
          trap 'rm -f "$key"' EXIT
          trap 'exit 1' INT TERM HUP
          printf '%s\n' "$NOTARY_KEY_P8" > "$key"
          unset NOTARY_KEY_P8
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$key" node scripts/notarize-dmg.mjs "${images[0]}" --log "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary-log/notary-log-$TARGET.json"

find:
# The refusal above sees only what landed in the download's own
      # folder. This holds the workspace itself to the checkout, still
      # before the key exists: at this run's commit, the checked-out files
      # as that commit has them, and nothing beside them, ignored names
      # included. A file that reached the workspace by any road, an archive
      # unpacked outside its folder among them, stops the job here. Git is
      # told to take nothing from the folder it is judging that would run a
      # program: no file-system monitor, no external diff, no conversion.
      - name: Refuse a workspace that is not this run's checkout
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git() { command git -c core.fsmonitor=false "$@"; }
          head=$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)
          if [ "$head" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
            echo "::error::the workspace is at commit ${head:0:12} and this run is for ${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}: it is not this run's checkout. Nothing was run, and the notary's key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git diff --quiet --no-ext-diff --no-textconv HEAD --; then
            git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored
            echo "::error::a checked-out file is not as the commit has it: something wrote over a script or the config this job is about to use with the notary's key. Nothing was run, and the key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          stray=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored)
          if [ -n "$stray" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$stray"
            echo "::error::the workspace holds what the checkout did not put there (listed above), beside the files this job is about to use with the notary's key. Nothing was run, and the key was not written"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "the workspace is the checkout of ${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}: its files as committed, and nothing beside them"

      # spctl's verdicts mean nothing on a machine where Gatekeeper's
      # assessments are off: everything is accepted, signed or not. A runner
      # image can come that way, so they are turned on here if they are off,
      # the status is said before and after, and only a runner where they
      # will not come on fails. macOS has spelt the option two ways.
      - name: Turn Gatekeeper's assessments on if they are off
        shell: bash
        run: |
          before=$(spctl --status 2>&1 || true)
          echo "Gatekeeper before: $before"
          if [[ "$before" != *'assessments enabled'* ]]; then
            sudo spctl --global-enable || sudo spctl --master-enable || true
          fi
          after=$(spctl --status 2>&1 || true)
          echo "Gatekeeper after: $after"
          if [[ "$after" != *'assessments enabled'* ]]; then
            echo "::error::Gatekeeper's assessments are off on this runner and could not be turned on, so spctl's verdicts here would prove nothing about the image"
            exit 1
          fi

      # The notary's key exists in this step alone: written to a file nobody
      # else can read, handed to the script by path, and removed when the
      # shell exits normally or fails; on a cancelled or timed-out step the
      # hosted runner is discarded with the file. The limit is past the
      # script's own worst case, so the script gives up first and says why:
      # 70 minutes for the submission (notarytool's 60 of waiting and the
      # upload before it), three tries of the log and three of the staple at
      # 2 minutes each with a quarter of a minute between tries, and 1 for
      # the validation, which is 84.
      - name: Notarise and staple the disk image
        timeout-minutes: 90
        shell: bash
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY_P8: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_P8 }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          images=("$RUNNER_TEMP/signed/release/"*.dmg)
          if [ "${#images[@]}" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::expected one disk image in the download's release folder, found ${#images[@]}"
            exit 1
          fi
          umask 077
          key="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary-key.p8"
          trap 'rm -f "$key"' EXIT
          trap 'exit 1' INT TERM HUP
          printf '%s\n' "$NOTARY_KEY_P8" > "$key"
          unset NOTARY_KEY_P8
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$key" node scripts/notarize-dmg.mjs "${images[0]}" --log "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary-log/notary-log-$TARGET.json"
